doc.add_heading("E. FOIA / public records (Comment #20; SL §3) — COMPROMISE", level=2)
P("We agree with you that the carve-out itself should be conceded; Meridian had one in Fund III and three public pensions received one at first close. The drafting must change. As marked, Meridian could disclose “any and all Fund information” with no notice, no protective treatment and no limit on scope, “in its sole discretion” where disclosure is “required, requested or appropriate”. It also asks the GP to waive injunctive relief and claims. That goes beyond Meridian’s own statute. MPRSTA requires a covered system to notify the Fund Manager within 5 business days of a MORA request touching Confidential Information and to withhold disclosure for up to 15 business days while the Fund Manager seeks protection (§24-51-210(b)). It protects portfolio trade secrets, pending deal terms, proprietary models and other investors’ identities and terms (§210(a)). It voids confidentiality restrictions only for information the Act requires to be disclosed (§209(b), §210(c)). MORA retains its own trade-secret exemption (§24-72-108; MPRSTA §212). Recommended side-letter formulation: (a) MPRSTA-mandated disclosures (§§204–208) are permitted without restriction; (b) other information may be disclosed only as required by law, after notice within 5 business days of the request and at least 10 business days before disclosure (Fund III and first-close precedent), with a window of up to 15 business days for the GP to seek protective treatment at its expense, and with Meridian asserting available exemptions and limiting disclosure to the minimum required; (c) no voluntary disclosure of other LPs’ identities or terms, portfolio-company trade secrets or pending-transaction terms. Delete the waivers. Set cooperation timing at 30 days (§204(c), §207(d)), not 5 business days. Correct the cross-reference: SL §3.2 cites “LPA Section 12.1”, which is the transfer provision in Fund IV.")

New LPA §4.3(f) would make Meridian’s right prevail over the LPAC policy. That conflicts with §8.6(b) and §9.6 and would force exactly the first-close renegotiation you want to avoid. Recommendation: offer a side-letter pro-rata right in the first-close form, with Meridian’s share at 125/1,800 = 6.94%, plus an annual pipeline conversation. One verification point first: the internal records conflict on whether first-close co-investments are fee-free and carry-free. The first-close tracker says standard fees and carry apply; term sheet §5 says no-fee/no-carry; the Fund III tracker shows fee-free co-investments, which term sheet §4 denies. Meridian’s SL §7.3 terms should match whatever the executed first-close letters provide, no better.")
